titolo: TensorLean formally verifies GPU kernels, finds bugs in FlashAttention and DeepGEMM
descr: Researchers from Columbia and CertiK launch TensorLean, a Lean‑based framework that proved 83 of 149 PTX kernels correct and uncovered 38 bugs.
paragrafi: TensorLean lets developers write a tensor‑level specification and then proves the kernel is data‑race free, terminates, and meets functional correctness within floating‑point tolerance.
The tool was applied to 149 open‑source kernel instances, including 102 from FlashAttention, and proved 83 of them correct.
It also identified 38 bugs across FlashAttention, DeepGEMM and other libraries, with 39 correctness bugs reported to developers.
The project is open‑source on GitHub and will soon publish a paper and full specifications of the verified kernels.
perche: TensorLean shows that formal methods can improve GPU kernel reliability, reducing silent memory errors and data races. For AI practitioners, more robust kernels mean fewer crashes and more predictable performance, which benefits both cloud and on‑premise deployments of large models.
